The Chauri Chaura incident was a significant event in the Indian independence movement.

Key details:

Occurred on February 5, 1922, in Chauri Chaura, United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh)

Involved a violent clash between protesters and police

Part of the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi

Protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen

This event led Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement

Demonstrated the potential for violence in the independence struggle

Highlighted Gandhi's commitment to non-violent resistance

Marked a turning point in the Indian independence movement

Ernest Rutherford's gold foil experiment was a groundbreaking scientific investigation in the field of atomic structure. He used an extremely thin gold foil (about 1000 atoms thick) to conduct his famous alpha particle scattering experiment.

Key points about the experiment:

Conducted in 1909

Aimed to understand the structure of atoms

Showed that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus

Disproved the "plum pudding" model of the atom

Demonstrated that most of an atom's mass is concentrated in a tiny nucleus

Led to the development of the modern understanding of atomic structure

The experiment involved shooting alpha particles at the gold foil and observing their behavior, which revealed that atoms are mostly empty space with a small, dense central nucleus.

questions.question: What do we mean by Allen's rule? एलन के नियम से हमारा क्या तात्पर्य है?
questions.solution:
Allen's rule is an ecological principle that describes how animal body shape adapts to different climates. Specifically, it focuses on how animals in colder regions have evolved physical characteristics that help them conserve body heat.

Key points about Allen's rule:

· It explains why mammals in cold regions tend to have:

o Shorter ears

o Shorter limbs

o More compact body shapes

· These adaptations help reduce surface area, which minimizes heat loss

· This is an example of how organisms adapt to their environmental conditions through evolutionary processes

Antoine Lavoisier was a French chemist who is often called the "Father of Modern Chemistry". In the 18th century, he made a groundbreaking contribution to our understanding of chemical reactions, particularly combustion.

Before Lavoisier, scientists believed in the phlogiston theory, which suggested that a substance called phlogiston was released during burning. Lavoisier challenged this theory by demonstrating that combustion is actually a chemical reaction involving oxygen. He showed that when substances burn, they combine with oxygen from the air, which was a revolutionary concept at the time.

The law-making process in India has been primarily influenced by the British Constitution because:

  • India's Parliamentary system of government (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha) follows the Westminster model of the UK.
  • The bicameral legislature, the concept of Rule of Law, and parliamentary sovereignty are derived from the British system.
  • The procedure for making laws, including debates, committee reviews, and assent by the President, is inspired by the British parliamentary process.

Thus, the British Constitution played a crucial role in shaping India's legislative system.

questions.question: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. All the chefs in the world are famous because of their _____________ skills.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank.

All the chefs in the world are famous because of their _____________ skills.
questions.solution: "Culinary" is the correct spelling. It means relating to cooking or kitchen activities. The word comes from the Latin "culinarius," meaning "related to the kitchen." Common uses include "culinary arts," "culinary school," and "culinary expertise."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. " Success is not a destination, it's a journey."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

"Success is not a destination, it's a journey."
questions.solution: "Success" means the accomplishment of an aim or purpose. Its direct antonym is "failure," which means lack of success or the inability to achieve desired results.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. "Nobody's fool"
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

"Nobody's fool"
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 - "Not easily deceived"

The idiom "nobody's fool" describes someone who is clever and cannot be easily tricked or deceived. This person is wise and aware enough to avoid being fooled by others. The other options either misinterpret the idiom or provide incorrect meanings.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. "He must deliver pizza."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

"He must deliver pizza."

options.text: Pizza has to be delivered by him.
options.html: Pizza has to be delivered by him.

options.text: Pizza have to be delivered by him.
options.html: Pizza have to be delivered by him.

options.text: Pizza must be delivered by him.
options.html: Pizza must be delivered by him.

options.text: Pizza can be delivered by him.
options.html: Pizza can be delivered by him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 - "Pizza must be delivered by him."

When converting from active to passive voice with modal verbs like "must," the modal verb remains unchanged, and the main verb changes to its past participle form. The subject ("he") becomes the object with the preposition "by," and the object ("pizza") becomes the subject. The other options are incorrect because they use improper modal verb combinations.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word "crux" to fill in the blank. "The________ of his argument was that education should continue throughout life."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word "crux" to fill in the blank.

"The________ of his argument was that education should continue throughout life."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 - "essence"

The word "crux" means the most important or decisive point of an issue. "Essence" most appropriately captures this meaning, referring to the fundamental or most important aspect of something. The other options do not convey the same meaning: "proposal" suggests a plan, "etiquette" refers to proper behavior, and "draft" indicates a preliminary version.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The letter was being typed by the secretary when the phone rang.
questions.questionHtml:

The letter was being typed by the secretary when the phone rang.

options.text: The secretary will type the letter when the phone rings.

questions.solution:
To convert from passive to active voice:

· Original (passive): "was being typed" (past continuous passive)

· Active form: "was typing" (past continuous active) The timing is maintained with "when the phone rang"

(P) an open mind

questions.question: Arrange the sentences in correct order. A. A big fancy dress ball was arranged to celebrate their homecoming. B. It must have been a terrible shock for a young girl. C. They had been married a month, just home from their honeymoon. D. Just as the guests were starting to arrive, Charnley locked himself into his bedroom and shot himself.
questions.questionHtml:
Arrange the sentences in correct order.

A. A big fancy dress ball was arranged to celebrate their homecoming.

B. It must have been a terrible shock for a young girl.

C. They had been married a month, just home from their honeymoon.

D. Just as the guests were starting to arrive, Charnley locked himself into his bedroom and shot himself.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 - BCAD.

Sentence B introduces the "terrible shock" as the central theme.

Sentence C provides the setup, introducing the couple and their circumstances.

Sentence A adds details about the celebration planned for them.

Sentence D delivers the shocking event that ties back to Sentence B.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. "She believed she had been blamed for the mistakes of others for what happened."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment.

"She believed she had been blamed for the mistakes of others for what happened."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 - "Made a scapegoat"

The phrase "made a scapegoat" precisely captures the meaning of being blamed for others' mistakes. A scapegoat is someone who is made to bear the blame for others' faults. The other options are unrelated: "made a sceptic" refers to becoming doubtful, "made a spinster" refers to an unmarried woman, and "made a savage" suggests becoming uncivilized.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Paramount
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Paramount
questions.solution:
"Paramount" means supreme, foremost, or of highest importance/rank.

The word "supreme" best captures this meaning as it also indicates the highest in authority, importance, or rank. Other options are either opposites (inferior, trivial) or unrelated (collateral).

questions.questionHtml:
In the following sentence, four words are underlined out of which one word is misspelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

I took out a water tumbler(A) for a drink, but found the water in the metal container (B) had frozen so I couldn't quanch (C) my thirst. I ate some biscuits and offered (D) some to Hillary.
questions.solution:
The word "quanch" is misspelled. The correct spelling is "quench" meaning to satisfy one's thirst. All other underlined words are spelled correctly:

· tumbler (A) - correct

· container (B) - correct

· quanch (C) - incorrect, should be "quench"

· offered (D) - correct

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bold word. "His eloquent speech always persuades people to work for their betterment."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bold word.

"His eloquent speech always persuades people to work for their betterment."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 - "Articulate"

"Eloquent" means fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing. "Articulate" most closely matches this meaning, referring to someone who expresses themselves clearly and effectively. The other options have contrasting meanings:

"Vague" means unclear

"Inarticulate" means unable to speak clearly

"Short" is unrelated to speaking ability

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A dime a dozen
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A dime a dozen
questions.solution: "A dime a dozen" is an idiom meaning something is very common, plentiful, and therefore not particularly valuable or special. The phrase comes from times when things were so plentiful they could be sold very cheaply (a dozen for a dime).

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Failing to give proper care and attention
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Failing to give proper care and attention
questions.solution:
"Lax" means not sufficiently strict, careful, or attentive. It perfectly captures the meaning of "failing to give proper care and attention." The other options have different meanings:

Cautious: careful and thoughtful

Wild: uncontrolled or untamed

Provident: careful in providing for the future

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. When I saw him , I will ask him to return the book he borrowed.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

When I saw him, I will ask him to return the book he borrowed.
questions.solution:
The sentence has an error in tense consistency. The first part uses past tense ("saw") while the second uses future tense ("will ask"), creating a logical time conflict. The correct version should maintain the same tense throughout. The present tense "see" works best here as it indicates a future condition:

The correct sentence is- "When I see him, I will ask him to return the book he borrowed."

questions.question: Select the part that contains an error. "Solutions to the country's interior problems are still a long way away."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the part that contains an error.

"Solutions to the country's interior problems are still a long way away."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 - "the country's interior"

The error is in the phrase "interior problems." The correct phrase should be "internal problems." Interior generally refers to the physical inside of something, while internal is used for problems or matters within an organization or country.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. "They secret / decided / to leave / the town."
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

"They secret / decided / to leave / the town."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 - "They secret"

The error is in the segment "They secret." The word "secret" is being used incorrectly as an adverb. The correct phrase should be "They secretly decided to leave the town." The other segments are grammatically correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Brittle
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Brittle
questions.solution:
"Brittle" means easily broken or damaged. Its antonym should be a word meaning strong or not easily broken. "Resilient" (able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions) is the perfect antonym.

The other options either:

Are synonyms (crunchy, delicate)

Are unrelated (aloof - emotionally distant)

"Among" is the appropriate preposition when referring to being part of a larger group. The other options ("through," "therefore," "onto") would not make logical sense in this context.

questions.solution:

"Marginalised" fits the context as it describes the social, economic, and cultural exclusion of the Adivasis. The other options do not convey the intended meaning of systematic disadvantage.

questions.solution:

"Poverty" logically completes the sentence as it is a condition that causes suffering and is often associated with marginalized communities. The other options do not fit the context of describing hardship.

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Out of those group members, Rohan is the one who opposes others , no matter what they tell him.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

Out of those group members, Rohan is the one who opposes others, no matter what they tell him.
questions.solution:
"Antagonist" means someone who actively opposes or is hostile to someone or something. It perfectly describes someone who consistently opposes others. The other options have different meanings:

· Agonist: a chemical that triggers a response in cells

· Anatomist: someone who studies anatomy

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Expertise
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Expertise
questions.solution: "Expertise" means expert skill or knowledge in a particular field. "Proficiency" (advanced skill or expertise) is the closest synonym. The other options are either antonyms (ignorance, clumsiness) or unrelated concepts (lack).
